subject.title: fix(agents): prevent recursive task execution during model fallback

question: Should a fallback turn triggered by a completion announcement lose all embedded `sessions_spawn` capability until a new explicit user instruction?
rationale: The patch implements that stronger fail-closed policy, while the stated invariant and parent announcement contract only prohibit re-executing or re-delegating the work already reported as completed.

options.title: Preserve valid continuation
options.body: Narrow the policy so announced-work replay is blocked while unrelated remaining steps of the original task can still be delegated.

options.title: Fail closed for the turn
options.body: Keep the blanket spawn denial and explicitly accept the compatibility change with upgrade and multi-step orchestration proof.

options.title: Wait for unified enforcement
options.body: Pause this PR until OpenClaw-owned spawn, send, and scheduling tools can share one coherent completion-turn policy.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid continuation
recommendation.body: Narrow the policy so announced-work replay is blocked while unrelated remaining steps of the original task can still be delegated.

likelyOwner.reason: He established the cross-harness invariant, is the current assignee, and is best positioned to accept or reject the staged policy boundary.
